who_grade.reasoning: For CNS WHO grade considered independently, the metadata strongly favor grade 4 behavior. ET Volume (mL), Proportion Enhancing, Thickness of enhancing margin, NCR Volume (mL), and Proportion Necrosis indicate enhancing and necrotic tumor components. Multifocal or Multicentric disease, Number of lesions, Multiple satellites present, Deep WM invasion, large Total tumor volume (mL), and high Proportion of Oedema further support high-grade aggressive disease. Features arguing against the highest grade include only Mild Enhancement Quality, T2-FLAIR Mismatch Present, and midline_shift_present recorded as no, which can be seen in lower-grade or less mass-effect-producing tumors. Overall, the enhancing/necrotic multifocal infiltrative phenotype most supports CNS WHO grade 4.
